body:
How much validation coverage is lost through test recognition, command selection and output parsing? Follow-up to #28; investigation remains open.

**Live targeting result:** a general selector excluding deleted test paths removes Matchms PR958's missing-file error, but both stages then stop during collection because historical code imports missing `chemap`. No task is recovered. PR671 preserves exact native sets under both selections: 1 fail-to-pass and 30 pass-to-pass tests. Transport, validator/parser, source/test patches and reconstructed image were held fixed; no dependency repair was applied.

**Other findings:** four of six predeclared SAMtools PRs add net Perl test invocations, while the pinned recognizer counts zero for all six. SGR normalization passes 12 fixtures in both native and exported parsers. Synthetic completion checks reject six incomplete/error cases accepted by upstream while preserving the complete case; they do not regrade original tasks. MNE's explicit broad target remains a separate selection issue.

**Remaining:** evaluate general runner support and MNE targeting, then exercise parser/completion candidates on frozen live cases. Any recovery claim requires complete positive controls. No per-PR command/dependency edits or additional LLM repair loop.

**Execution:** one live job, one attempt, 0.22337 allocated CPU-hours against a 10-hour ceiling, zero model calls. Owned resources are removed and archive readback verified. Raw Matchms evidence stays private; reconstruction drift limits historical equivalence. No exports or independent Harbor controls were generated by this comparison.

[Live diagnosis](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/40a80ef0/experiments/32-runner-coverage/target-live-diagnosis.json) · [Archive/cleanup verification](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/40a80ef0/experiments/32-runner-coverage/live-readback.json) · [Selection checks](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/40a80ef0/experiments/32-runner-coverage/deleted-target-results.json) · [Full scope](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/40a80ef0/experiments/32-runner-coverage/issue-scope.md). Detailed logs remain in comments.

comments.body:
🤖 Initial investigation is published on the permanent research branch at `0a875d9c899e4a1c4015c1e1ce47c96711ee1745`.

A predeclared six-PR SAMtools sample contains four PRs adding net Perl test invocations; the pinned recognizer counts zero for all six. All test-path sets agree with retained descriptors, but current diff bytes are not claimed identical to original unretained diffs. SGR normalization passes 12 explicit parser fixtures; two targeting checks reproduce preservation of MNE’s broad path.

Parser normalization alone is insufficient: partial timed-out logs can still contain apparent failure-to-pass transitions. The completion comparison uses exact native logic with synthetic executor outcomes and the real pinned pytest parser. Original rewards remain untouched. Raw sampled diffs stay local because they contain biological fixtures; public findings contain source URLs, paths, refs and hashes only.

Next: evaluate general runner/targeting changes and complete execution checks before live recovery claims. Seven synthetic validation cases show the pinned validator accepting six incomplete/error cases; a candidate completion guard rejects them while preserving the complete pair. This is mechanism evidence, not regrading of original tasks.

[Evidence](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/0a875d9c899e4a1c4015c1e1ce47c96711ee1745/experiments/32-runner-coverage/sample-findings.json) · [Scope](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/0a875d9c899e4a1c4015c1e1ce47c96711ee1745/experiments/32-runner-coverage/issue-scope.md) · [Logbook](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/0a875d9c899e4a1c4015c1e1ce47c96711ee1745/experiments/32-runner-coverage/logbook.md). All changes remain research-only; no promotion to main, live task repair or model spend. The issue remains open.

🤖 The styling-normalization candidate now covers both the native pytest parser and the exported standalone verifier. A native-only change could recognize statuses during generation that the eventual task grader still misreads.

All 12 expected-status fixtures pass for both candidate parsers, including plain-output parity with the pinned baselines and colored-output agreement. Normalization strips only ANSI SGR styling; it does not change test IDs, broaden terminal control handling, or prove that a test command finished. The separate completion guard and live comparisons remain required. No original task was regraded, and no model calls or remote jobs were launched for #32.

[Exact fixture results](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/0d38f3e76bbfeba803fa42bc5a026d688ec0d873/experiments/32-runner-coverage/parser-results.json), [exported-parser patch](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/0d38f3e76bbfeba803fa42bc5a026d688ec0d873/experiments/32-runner-coverage/sgr-export-parser.patch), [native-parser patch](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/0d38f3e76bbfeba803fa42bc5a026d688ec0d873/experiments/32-runner-coverage/sgr-parser.patch).

🤖 A live #30 comparison exposed another upstream targeting failure: Matchms PR958 deletes two test files, but the unchanged targeting function includes both deleted paths in the pytest command. Both pre/post stages report a missing test path and collect zero tests. The transport candidate removes errno7 but cannot produce F2P tests under that command.

The frozen patch and actual stdout hashes are bound in [the diagnosis](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/4862b97e/experiments/30-script-transport/live-diagnosis.json). No per-PR test repair was applied. This is a concrete case for a general diff-aware target-selection comparison under this issue, separate from color parsing and timeout completion checks. Removing deleted targets may expose further failures; recovery is not assumed.

🤖 Submitted the first #32 live comparison, `/exedev/biotasks32-matchms-targets-001`, after checkpointing the generic deleted-path selector, four arms and all inputs. It is currently running. Both arms use #30's stdin transport and the unchanged native validator/parser; only path selection differs. PR958 uses eight versus six targets; PR671's command is unchanged.

Local checks passed ten path fixtures, four runner fixtures, two frozen patch selections, complete source imports and all generated stage hashes/syntax. The selector changes both native and export targeting call sites, preserving reset/inventory extraction. No per-PR exception or manual command edit is present.

[Protocol and limits](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/d3de9d30/experiments/32-runner-coverage/protocol.md): one attempt, existing reserved capacity, at most 10 allocated CPU-hours, zero model calls. Native outcomes will be reported separately from recovered exports and independent controls. No live result is claimed yet.

🤖 The deleted-target comparison completed in one attempt: 201.029 seconds, 0.2233656 allocated CPU-hours, zero model calls. Archive and owned-resource cleanup are verified.

Original selection reproduces a missing test path and zero collected tests. The general surviving-path selector removes that error, but exposes missing `chemap`: pre collects 0 items with 6 errors; post collects 45 items with 5 errors. Both stop during collection and native validation returns no F2P tests. Collected items are not passing tests. No dependency installation or other repair was added.

PR671 preserves exactly the same native F2P/P2P sets (1/30). No exports or independent Harbor controls were generated, and no task-recovery claim is made. This isolates a real selection defect from a separate historical-environment failure.

[Diagnosis](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/40a80ef0/experiments/32-runner-coverage/target-live-diagnosis.json) · [Verified archive and cleanup](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/40a80ef0/experiments/32-runner-coverage/live-readback.json). Parser/completion and broader runner work remain open; the original comparisons remain immutable.
